summary:
Jonathan Davis, 28, had an unremarkable prior history involving his left shoulder — a July 2022 low-speed motorcycle fall resulting in a Grade I/II AC joint sprain and mild rotator cuff tendinitis, resolved with a 12-session course of physical therapy. That injury bears no relation to what followed on January 8, 2024, when Davis's left arm was crushed by an industrial metal stamping press at the NSK plant. Liberty County EMS Rescue 14 responded at 12:45, found the arm entrapped, applied a tourniquet, administered IV Fentanyl 100mcg, and transported him to Midwest Regional Medical Center, where he was triaged at ESI Level 1 with a blood pressure of 88/50, heart rate 130, and 10/10 pain — the physiology of a man in traumatic shock from catastrophic blood loss.

Imaging confirmed the clinical picture was as bad as it looked: X-ray and CT angiography revealed comminuted open segmental fractures of the forearm and hand, a comminuted displaced supracondylar humerus fracture, and complete cessation of contrast enhancement in the brachial artery at the distal third of the humerus. The limb was unsalvageable. After emergent transfusion of 2 units PRBC, Dr. Sarah Chen performed an emergent left transhumeral amputation with myofascial closure, bone beveling, and traction-neurectomy of the median, ulnar, and radial nerves; estimated blood loss was 650 mL. Postoperative labs showed leukocytosis (WBC 14.2) and anemia (Hgb 8.9, Hct 27.2). He was managed on a Dilaudid PCA, Gabapentin, and Ancef, and discharged after a 7-day admission on Gabapentin 300mg BID and Oxycodone.

The stump healed, but by the one-month follow-up Davis was suffering severe phantom limb pain rated 8/10, prompting an increase to Gabapentin 600mg TID and referral for desensitization therapy and prosthetic fitting. By June 2024 a tender 1.5cm mobile nodule had developed at the distal medial stump, diagnosed as a traumatic neuroma of the ulnar/median nerve stump, surgically excised on November 12, 2024 with proximal nerve transposition and embedding into the triceps.

Rehabilitation was then delayed nearly a month by a Liberty Mutual authorization hold on the proposed myoelectric prosthesis, but by February 2025 Davis was fitted with a custom carbon-fiber transhumeral prosthesis with a Utah Myoelectric Elbow and Motion Control MC Hand, achieving 80% electrode accuracy at delivery. Over ten PT visits spanning February 2025 through June 2026 — interrupted by two no-shows attributed to workload and transportation — his pain steadily declined from 5/10 to 1/10 while function climbed from basic electrode practice to fine motor screw manipulation and heavy-carrying simulation. He was discharged June 22, 2026 with master-level prosthetic control, independent ADLs, driving ability, 25-lb carrying capacity, and clearance to return to modified light/medium duty at NSK.
